verdict: Revise. The document-form hierarchy is generally coherent, and all internal-node representative probes synthesize their direct children, but generic schema filling and arbitrary format obedience have been mistaken for technical documentation. Several prerequisite edges also fail the rubric’s full-outcome necessity test.
blocking_findings: Containment failure: c23.reference.structured-records trains generic schema-constrained data encoding, not API or reference documentation. Its own outcome makes a structured instance—not documentation—the deliverable, and discovery tasks c23-d01, c23-d05, c23-d09, c23-d13, and c23-d16 are climate, invoice, interaction, housing, and camping records whose decisive operation is JSON Schema validation. The curriculum should reject or rehome this cluster rather than expand C23 around its output format.

Containment and boundary failure: c23.quality.constraints is broad enough to absorb arbitrary instruction-following. Discovery tasks c23-d02 and c23-d06 principally require implementing unrelated FFmpeg/Bash and DOM/JavaScript fixes; bigram wrapping, capitalization, paragraph counts, and boundary words do not turn those programming tasks into technical-writing tasks. The section needs a documentation-specific transformation boundary and probes whose supplied content is already technically complete.

Generation and mutual-confidence failure: c23.guides.explanations does not consistently isolate explanatory writing from technical problem solving. Its representative probe requires unstated knowledge and measurements about mutable-collection iteration, while discovery tasks c23-d04 and c23-d15 require different JavaScript expertise. Without supplying verified behavior, alternatives, and measurements, success measures domain recall and solution design rather than the claimed documentation outcome.

Prerequisite-continuity failure: seven explicit edges are either unnecessary at full-outcome strength or insufficient for the dependent entry task: c23.planning→c23.reference.operations, c23.planning.structure→c23.reference.data-models, c23.planning.structure→c23.reference.product-specifications, c23.planning.evidence→c23.reference.structured-records, c23.planning→c23.guides.how-to, c23.planning.structure→c23.design.proposals, and c23.planning.structure→c23.quality.constraints.
mutual_confidence_findings: c23.quality.constraints: compare c23-d02, which requires shell quoting and an FFmpeg timestamp overlay, with c23-d06, which requires DOM traversal, escaping, bookmarklet serialization, and download generation. Mastering either central implementation problem would not predict success on the other; the shared artificial prose constraints are peripheral. These tasks therefore cannot jointly anchor a mutually confident documentation section.

c23.guides.explanations: compare c23-d04, which requires knowledge of live DOM collections, mutation, iteration semantics, and performance qualification, with c23-d15, which requires knowledge of DOMContentLoaded, legacy-browser readiness fallbacks, and run-once event handling. Mastery of one does not transfer to the other because the prompts omit the technical evidence that would reduce both to the claimed explanatory operation.

c23.reference.structured-records itself is internally more coherent than the two sections above: c23-d01 and c23-d16 differ greatly in nesting and domain but share fact-to-field mapping, enum choice, JSON encoding, and schema validation. Its defect is subject containment, not a demonstrated need to split the schema skill further.
continuity_findings: c23.planning→c23.reference.operations is unnecessary at full strength. The dependent entry task only needs a verified interface definition and a reader; it does not exercise the prerequisite’s content inventory, claim-control, page hierarchy, navigation, or document-type selection outcomes. The minimal new delta—turning one operation into purpose/input/result reference prose—should follow narrower audience and evidence prerequisites.

c23.planning.structure→c23.reference.data-models and c23.planning.structure→c23.reference.product-specifications are unnecessary at full strength. Their representative tasks require orderly field or category presentation, but not reader-task page boundaries, progressive disclosure, navigation, and cross-reference planning. The evidence edges are useful; the full information-architecture edge is not.

c23.planning.evidence→c23.reference.structured-records is insufficient. Even the entry task adds fact-to-field mapping, JSON syntax, schema interpretation, required-field checking, type and enum checking, and policy-governed choices for missing values. That is several unmodeled capabilities rather than the smallest learnable delta from claim classification.

c23.planning→c23.guides.how-to is unnecessarily broad. The entry task needs a defined reader and supplied three-action procedure, then adds ordering and a completion check; it does not require a content inventory, claim-to-evidence map, document hierarchy, navigation, or document-type selection.

c23.planning.structure→c23.design.proposals is unnecessary. Given one requirement and two supplied approaches, the entry task adds comparison on a tradeoff and a recommendation; neither it nor the representative probe requires the full navigation and cross-reference outcome of information architecture. c23.design.requirements→c23.design.proposals supplies the material prerequisite.

c23.planning.structure→c23.quality.constraints is unnecessary. Reformatting one supplied note under a title, section-count, and final-line rule adds constraint parsing, meaning preservation, and compliance checking; it does not depend on reader-task information architecture.

The remaining explicit edges have plausible minimal deltas: c23.planning.audience→c23.planning.structure adds task-aligned hierarchy; c23.planning→c23.reference adds reference rendering; c23.planning.evidence→c23.reference.data-models and →c23.reference.product-specifications add contract semantics or normalized specification form; c23.planning→c23.guides adds instructional drafting; c23.guides.how-to plus c23.planning.audience→c23.guides.tutorials adds learning scaffolding; c23.planning.audience plus c23.planning.evidence→c23.guides.explanations adds qualified causal comparison; c23.guides.how-to plus c23.planning.evidence→c23.guides.troubleshooting adds diagnostic branching; c23.planning→c23.design adds measurable design framing; c23.planning.audience plus c23.planning.evidence→c23.design.requirements adds atomic verifiability; c23.design.requirements→c23.design.proposals adds option evaluation; c23.design.proposals→c23.design.decisions adds a settled choice and consequences; c23.planning→c23.quality adds controlled delivery; c23.planning.audience plus c23.planning.evidence→c23.quality.revision adds reader-specific disambiguation; and c23.quality.revision→c23.quality.maintenance adds propagation of a known change through references and version information.
other_findings: Discovery-evidence gap, separate from curriculum defects: of 16 discovery tasks, c23-d03, c23-d07, c23-d11, and c23-d14 are legal questions outside C23; five are generic schema-instance generation; c23-d02 and c23-d06 are programming tasks decorated with format constraints. The remaining evidence is concentrated in JavaScript explanations/troubleshooting and one product specification. There is no direct discovery support for documentation planning, API-operation reference, data-model reference, tutorials, requirements, design proposals, decision records, technical revision, or maintenance.

Evaluation-evidence gap, separate from curriculum defects: no eval manifest entry lists C23; all 15 entries list only C01, C07, C25, or C27. Consequently none of the individual eval annotations or tasks is permissible as C23 coverage or routing evidence. AAII 4.3 was treated as metadata-only.

All six internal nodes have coherent cross-child representative tasks: c23 integrates planning, reference, instruction, design, and maintenance around one product change; c23.planning combines audience, evidence, and structure; c23.reference combines operations, models, product facts, and configuration; c23.guides forms a cross-referenced support set; c23.design carries requirements through proposal to decision; and c23.quality combines compliance, revision, and change propagation.

The boundaries between c23.reference.product-specifications and c23.design.requirements, and between c23.guides.how-to and c23.guides.tutorials, are concrete and operational. The former distinguishes verified current-product facts from desired future behavior; the latter distinguishes task completion from scaffolded learning.
rubric_changes: Add a cross-subject containment rule that assigns a task by its decisive or hardest operation, not its answer format or incidental constraints. Schema-valid JSON, boxed answers, file delivery, paragraph counts, and lexical wrappers should not create subject coverage when the central operation belongs elsewhere.

Add a cross-subject probe-isolation rule: when an outcome claims transformation, explanation, revision, or documentation skill rather than domain expertise, the probe must supply the necessary facts, interface definition, causal model, measurements, or completed solution. Otherwise mutual-confidence judgments are confounded by unrelated knowledge.

Require reviews to report evidence sufficiency by subject and evidence class: guideposts, discovery tasks, applicable held-out probes, and metadata-only sources. Absence of applicable eval probes should be recorded as a confidence limitation rather than silently treated as positive or negative curriculum evidence.
